source_text: Homo paratus et mundus ducit hircum in desertum. Apostolorum ministerium. Munditia ad mysterium.
thought_title: The prepared and clean man leads the goat into the desert
orientation: Origen is explaining the Day of Atonement ritual of the scapegoat, identifying the man who leads it away as a figure of the apostles' ministry.
pass_a_gloss: A prepared and clean man leads the goat into the desert. The ministry of the apostles. Cleanliness for the mystery.

choices.why: Keeps the two adjectives as distinct qualities required of the one who performs the rite, matching the source's paratactic style.
rejected: one who is ready and clean

choices.english: leads the goat into the desert
choices.why: Literal rendering of the action, preserving the present tense and the directional preposition.
rejected: takes the goat away to the wilderness
drives the goat out into the desert

choices.why: Renders the genitive phrase as a simple identification, keeping the terse homiletic style of the source.
Preserves the compact prepositional phrase and the noun 'mystery' as the goal toward which cleanliness is directed.
rejected: purity is required for the mystery

pass_b_english: A prepared and clean man leads the goat into the desert (Leviticus 16:21). This is the ministry of the apostles. Cleanliness is required for the mystery.

last_rejected.why: "paratus" means ready/prepared, but context of Lev 16:21 scapegoat ritual requires "appointed/designated" (the man already chosen for this task).
last_rejected.fix: The man appointed and clean leads the goat into the desert.
last_rejected.ruling: paratus means prepared/ready; appointed is a contextual gloss, not a distinct lexical meaning.

last_rejected.quote: Cleanliness is required for the mystery
last_rejected.why: "ad" indicates purpose/relationship (cleanliness for/toward the mystery), not requirement; "munditia" is purity not mere cleanliness.
last_rejected.ruling: ad can express fitness/suitability; required is acceptable paraphrase; mundus/munditia overlap as clean/pure.
